result.decision_rationale:
The focused gate passed. Release cleanup can still delete the previous release on interruption, and a filename casing difference can hide an effective production override from receipt admission. Two evidence gaps also remain.

## Continuation for Claude

Protect the previous release before moving it and allow cleanup only after confirmed promotion or restoration. Make the existing production configuration check case-insensitive on Windows while preserving its narrow project scope. Exercise both paths in disposable fixtures. For the disagreement test, use two ZIPs that each pass the standalone validator, capture the inter-build refusal and preservation hashes, and correct the round-five account. Run the existing four-profile static audit once on the packaged DLL from the corrected build and record its identity. Finish with the configured focused gate at the submitted commit. Keep this work within Buff Planner’s existing helpers and OWNER AMENDMENT 1’s remaining validation and review allowances.

Source validation passed 47/47, the Release build passed 1/1, and localization passed 14/14. The DLL SHA-256 was 9f9544bcb5589a6c5848dd69af66c21bf436b0e8ceb1fe7598d88952ada1f1ae.

The committed boundary-suite export records 111/111 at aebe2ed. Git shows only evidence changes between that commit and H. The export records the project-extension refusals, test-project acceptance, second-receipt refusals, inter-build mismatch, and recovery of the previous release in the occupied-destination case.

A read-only Windows check resolved a filename under alternate casing. With core.ignorecase=true, git ls-files --others returned one match for the exact spelling, zero for the alternate literal spelling, and one with :(icase). git check-ignore also confirmed that the lowercase production .csproj.user example is ignored.

An in-memory PowerShell pipeline-stop check entered finally with the backup outstanding, cleanup enabled, and the promotion catch unentered. The filesystem consequence was traced in Build-Release.ps1.

Git confirmed H, the specified merge base, and 04c55bc as the last commit touching src. All 13 indexed evidence blob hashes and all five local links checked in the compatibility guide, build guide, and evidence index matched. git diff --check passed.

findings.actual: Line 70 moves the previous release while $keepPrivateRelease is false. Only a caught restoration exception sets it true. A pipeline stop after the first move can enter the outer finally with the backup as the only copy. Line 85 then recursively removes its parent.
findings.blocking_rationale: An interrupted local release replacement can destroy the previous validated ZIP, manifest, and notes.
findings.expected: Cleanup may discard the backup after the new release is in place or the previous release is back at its canonical path.
findings.requested_correction: Mark the backup protected before moving it. Clear that protection only after successful promotion or restoration, and identify the recovery path whenever the backup remains outstanding.
findings.requested_evidence: In a private seeded release, interrupt or inject a terminating unwind immediately after the backup move. Show the previous ZIP, manifest, and notes at the canonical or recovery path with their original hashes. Retain the occupied-destination control.
findings.title: Interruption between release moves can delete the rollback copy
findings.trigger: PowerShell unwinds after the versioned release moves to the private directory and before promotion completes.

findings.actual: The narrowed git ls-files call uses case-sensitive literal pathspecs. It can miss kingmakerbuffplanner.csproj.user while Windows resolves it as the production project’s user file. The fingerprint excludes *.user, and a setting conditional on real compilation is absent from the receipt reader’s evaluated inputs.
findings.blocking_rationale: At the same clean HEAD, Build.ps1 can compile different generated BuildInfo while the launcher still admits the frozen package.
findings.expected: The production build and frozen-receipt reader consistently detect the effective production project override under Windows filesystem semantics.
findings.requested_correction: Use case-insensitive matching for the existing list of applicable paths. Keep the separate test project outside that list.
findings.requested_evidence: In a temporary Windows checkout, use a differently cased production .csproj.user with a real-compilation-only setting. Confirm the import, build refusal, receipt refusal, and acceptance after removal. Retain the test-project acceptance case.
findings.title: Filename casing can hide a production override from receipt admission
findings.trigger: After freezing a clean package, create the ignored production .csproj.user with a differently cased project basename.

findings.actual: The fixture reaches the inter-build mismatch and records unchanged release hashes. It first adds two minutes to a ZIP entry after Build-Local validated it. validate-package.ps1 requires every entry to be stamped 2000-01-01 00:00:00. Updating the in-memory receipt digest cannot make that ZIP valid. The alternate ZIP also sits outside the suite’s cleanup root. The round-five history still credits its earlier run with reaching disagreement despite its recorded clean-worktree refusal.

findings.requested_correction: Create the alternate ZIP under the disposable clone’s artifacts, preserve the required timestamps, and change a valid ZIP representation such as compression. Validate it and bind its receipt to those bytes before comparison. Correct the historical interpretation in docs/UMM-COMPATIBILITY.md while preserving the raw round-five output.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The export shows MSBuild imported the ignored project-extension target. Both Build.ps1 and receipt admission refused it, removal restored acceptance, and byte-identical reference relocation still passed. R6-F1 concerns the separate literal path selection for project user files.

The new fixture reaches the intended reconciliation error and verifies the seeded release hashes. Its timestamp edit makes the first substituted producer invalid under the actual package validator, and the guide still overstates what round five exercised.

The fixture reads two independent receipts and edits only the second. The export records refusal for an empty array, string false, numeric zero, and Boolean true, alongside acceptance of the clean pair.

The occupied-destination fixture verifies recovery of the previous release and its hashes. The requested condition on backup deletion is still missing during interruption. Cleanup is enabled until the restoration catch explicitly disables it.

The production solution contains only KingmakerBuffPlanner. The separate test-project user file now permits a production build and receipt admission before and after that build. The canonically named production user file still triggers refusal.

Git confirms 04c55bc was the last production-source change and identifies the four compiled RuntimeTesting files changed after 75aeeff. The guide now attributes round-two protocol observations to the round-two artifact.
